summary: A [National Strategy for Digital Governance](2024-01-01 National Strategy for Digital Governance in São Tomé and Príncipe) adopted in 2020 runs on nine thematic axes, and a [Public Administration Reform Strategy](2025-06-18-ministra-justica-digitalizacao-setor-publico) approved in 2025 names electronic governance its essential pillar.
developments:
The digital governance strategy is a whole-of-government instrument on nine axes; the source page is undated and the year is taken from its context, so even the strategy's own date rests on inference ([strategy](2024-01-01 National Strategy for Digital Governance in São Tomé and Príncipe)).

The reform strategy was presented as newly approved in June 2025 with electronic governance named as its essential pillar ([reform](2025-06-18-ministra-justica-digitalizacao-setor-publico)).

Neither carries a target, budget, milestone or review published anywhere the base can reach, so what either instrument commits the state to is unstated.

summary: A [revision of the regulatory framework](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) covering the regulatory entities law and the electronic communications law was approved by the Council of Ministers and sent to the National Assembly.
developments:
The regulator's own statute was already approved, and the two laws went to the Assembly in 2025; no later source confirms parliamentary passage ([revision](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

That is the whole of the record. A regulatory framework sitting with the legislature for a year with nothing published about its progress is the standing condition of most legislative items in this unit.

summary: A [data governance capacity building workshop](2026-07-13 D4D Hub on Sao Tome and Principe) was held in July 2026 as part of adopting the continental data policy framework nationally.
developments:
The workshop ran over two days with a European development hub, a continental development agency and a regional civil-society network ([workshop](2026-07-13 D4D Hub on Sao Tome and Principe)).

No national policy, adoption decision or timetable follows it. Adoption of the continental framework is at the stage of officials being trained on it.

summary: A [personal data protection law of 2016](2024-01-01 São Tomé and Príncipe - Digital Regulations in the Metaverse Era (Data)) modelled on a superseded European directive is enforced by the national authority, and the primary text is not held.
developments:
The enactment year is taken from the law's own designation, and the only source describing it is a 2024 secondary legal survey rather than the 2016 text ([law](2024-01-01 São Tomé and Príncipe - Digital Regulations in the Metaverse Era (Data))).

Modelling on a directive that Europe itself replaced in 2018 is the substantive point: the regime the authority enforces is two generations behind the standard its cooperation partners now work to.

The country is a signatory to the continental cyber and data convention, with ratification status not stated ([convention](2024-01-01 São Tomé and Príncipe - Digital Regulations in the Metaverse Era (Data))).

summary: A [National Framework for Interoperability](2024-01-01 São Tomé and Príncipe - Digital Regulations in the Metaverse Era (Data)) was enacted as Law 1/2024 for public-sector data sharing, and only a secondary legal survey describes it.
developments:
The law is held through the same 2024 legal-survey chapter as the data-protection law, not through its own text ([law](2024-01-01 São Tomé and Príncipe - Digital Regulations in the Metaverse Era (Data))).

It is the legal basis for the civil-registry to electoral-database linkage recorded separately, which is the one working interoperability in this unit — so the law has an evidenced use even though its provisions cannot be read here.

summary: An [aggregated identification document law](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) was flagged as urgent by a lender mission in 2025, its absence stated as a potential constraint on data collection, and no later source confirms passage.
developments:
The mission flagged review, public consultation, finalisation and approval as urgent ([law](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

A year later nothing records movement. The foundational digital identity it would govern has live prototypes and a system integrator engaged, so the build is running ahead of the statute — the same order this frame finds in most units.

summary: The authority was [assigned to supervise the civil-registry to electoral-database interconnection](2026-04-15-recenseamento-automatico-fiscalizado-anpdp), and [signed a cooperation memorandum with a Macau counterpart](2026-06-10-dspdp-macau-formaliza-cooperacao-protecao-dados-stp) covering cross-border flows and artificial-intelligence supervision.
developments:
Supervision of the interconnection was assigned in April 2026, which is the only instance in this base of a data-protection authority being given oversight of a specific interoperability project at the point it goes live ([supervision](2026-04-15-recenseamento-automatico-fiscalizado-anpdp)).

The memorandum was signed in June 2026 covering cross-border data flows, artificial-intelligence supervision, awareness, training and joint studies ([memorandum](2026-06-10-dspdp-macau-formaliza-cooperacao-protecao-dados-stp), [pacts](2026-05-27-macau-to-sign-data-protection-pacts-stp-cabo-verde)).

The authority is also a founding member of a recently created Lusophone data-protection network, hosted for a cooperation visit by the Portuguese commission ([network](2025-06-23-cnpd-portugal-recebeu-anpdp-stp-rede-lusofona)). Its supervisory output — findings, penalties, registrations — is not published at any date.

summary: The country is one of seven covered by a [programme for African developing island economies](2026-07-24-auda-nepad-island-economies-programme-launch), and takes part in a [Lusophone data governance workshop series](2026-07-28-advancing-data-infrastructure-and-governance-in-lusophone-africa) and [regional digital governance dialogues](2026-03-31-palop-digital-identity-collaboration-biometricupdate).
developments:
The island economies programme was launched at a ministerial segment in July 2026; it is a seven-state programme and no national commitments beyond the communique are detailed ([programme](2026-07-24-auda-nepad-island-economies-programme-launch)).

A second Lusophone data governance workshop was held in June 2026, and the country's specific national content from it is not detailed ([workshop](2026-07-28-advancing-data-infrastructure-and-governance-in-lusophone-africa)).

A second webinar in the regional digital governance series covered digital identity as foundational infrastructure, again from a multi-country source with no national content separated out ([dialogues](2026-03-31-palop-digital-identity-collaboration-biometricupdate)). Three regional forums, and in none of them can the base say what this country said or undertook.

summary: A [first internet governance forum](2026-07-31-ager-1a-edicao-fgi-stp-sao-tome) was held over three days in July 2026, opened by the prime minister.
developments:
The first edition was convened by the regulator and opened by the head of government ([forum](2026-07-31-ager-1a-edicao-fgi-stp-sao-tome)).

No outcome document, participant count or commitment is published. It is the only multi-stakeholder convening in this ledger, and it is a first edition, so nothing yet establishes whether it becomes a standing channel.

summary: A [lender digital project](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) had disbursed 36 per cent by September 2025 at a moderately satisfactory rating, and it finances almost everything else in this ledger.
developments:
The project finances the digital identity, the citizen portal, the interoperability platform, the incident response team and the data-centre work ([project](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025), [approval](2022-06-15-wb-stp-001-digital-sao-tome-and-principe)).

That concentration is the finding: a single donor operation is the delivery vehicle for the state's entire digital programme, and its September 2025 mission report is also the only source for four separate items recorded here.

A payment system and financial inclusion grant of about US$3.34m has been active since 2017 ([grant](2017-01-01-afdb-stp-001-sao-tome-and-principe---payments)); the disbursed figure in the source exceeds the committed figure with no explanation found ([grant](2017-01-01-afdb-stp-001-sao-tome-and-principe---payments)).

summary: The incumbent operator [inaugurated its 35th antenna](2026-03-27-cst-inaugura-antena-agua-ize) in March 2026, on a network expansion running alongside a school connectivity plan.
developments:
The 35th antenna was inaugurated in a coastal district in March 2026 ([antenna](2026-03-27-cst-inaugura-antena-agua-ize), [expansion](2025-01-25-cst-35-anos-expansao-rede-conectividade-escolas)).

No coverage percentage, subscriber count or population-served figure accompanies it, so the antenna count is the only measure of the network the base holds. For a two-island state, a count of masts is a more meaningful measure than it would be elsewhere, and it is still not coverage.

summary: [Satellite internet service was activated](2025-12-11-starlink-begins-service-stp) in December 2025, about ten months after the operator stated an intention to invest.
developments:
Intention to invest was reported in February 2025 and service began in December ([service](2025-12-11-starlink-begins-service-stp), [intention](2025-02-24-starlink-pretende-investir-stp-eua)).

No licence terms, subscriber count, tariff or regulatory condition is published. In an island state whose only submarine cable to its second island is still in build, satellite is the redundancy that arrived first.

summary: A [submarine cable to the second island](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) is listed as an active project objective, and no source states its build status or a completion date.
developments:
It is monitored as an objective of the lender's digital project ([cable](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

No build status or completion date is held. Connecting the smaller island is the single most consequential connectivity item for this country, and the base can say only that it remains an objective.

summary: The procurement agency [tendered servers and disaster recovery](2026-05-14-afap-tender-data-center-servidores-identidade-digital) for the digital identity data centre, and the decision is not confirmed.
developments:
The tender covers servers and a disaster recovery arrangement for the identity data centre, inside a wider government data-centre modernisation ([tender](2026-05-14-afap-tender-data-center-servidores-identidade-digital), [mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

The tender's own body is an attached document that has not been read, so scope, value and specification are unstated. No award or decision is confirmed.

That a disaster recovery arrangement is being procured alongside the primary is worth noting: it is the only redundancy design named anywhere in this ledger.

summary: An [incident response team](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) appears as a lender mission objective — its materialisation to be launched — on a single line in one report with no later source.
developments:
The mission listed launching the team's materialisation as an objective in September 2025 ([team](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

Nothing since. A single line in one donor mission report is the entire cybersecurity record for this country: no strategy, no statute, no incident, no capability figure appears anywhere else in this ledger.

summary: The procurement agency [extended the deadline on a tender](2026-08-07-afap-prorroga-solicitacao-novo-sistema-de-informacao-de-gestao-mis-para-a-emae) for a new management information system for the electricity and water utility.
developments:
The tender covers supply, installation, training and commissioning; the notice is a scanned document with no text layer and only its headline is readable, so scope and value are unstated ([tender](2026-08-07-afap-prorroga-solicitacao-novo-sistema-de-informacao-de-gestao-mis-para-a-emae)).

An extended deadline usually indicates insufficient qualifying bids, though nothing on file says so. It is the only utility system in this ledger, and the grid it would manage is the one every data centre and antenna in the country depends on.

summary: A [foundational digital identity on an open-source platform](2025-06-05 São Tomé and Principe pilots MOSIP-based national digital ID system) has live prototypes for credentials, data exchange, portal and electronic signature, and no source confirms the card itself has launched.
developments:
A system integrator is engaged with the identity institute and the registries directorate, with prototypes live and a roadmap running January to May 2026 ([pilot](2025-06-05 São Tomé and Principe pilots MOSIP-based national digital ID system), [mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

No source held confirms the foundational card has launched, and the roadmap's delivery is not confirmed either. The identification law that would govern it was flagged as urgent in 2025 and has not passed.

So the components exist as prototypes, the statute does not exist, and whether the thing itself is issued is unestablished.

summary: A [free national identity card campaign](2026-01-22-campanha-bi-gratuito-ilheu-das-rolas) ran in phases including an islet and a diaspora arm, with cards collectable at the embassy in Portugal.
developments:
The campaign ran to an outlying islet in January 2026 and extended to the diaspora, with cards collectable at the embassy in Portugal by June ([campaign](2026-01-22-campanha-bi-gratuito-ilheu-das-rolas), [diaspora](2026-06-25-bi-disponiveis-levantamento-campanha-diaspora-portugal), [embassy](2025-04-07-governo-lanca-sistema-emissao-documentos-embaixada-portugal)).

Free issuance and physical collection at an embassy are the two access designs that matter most in a small island state with a large diaspora, and both are recorded here.

No issuance count, coverage figure or campaign end date is published.

summary: A [passport issuance system](2026-04-15-stp-lanca-sistema-emissao-passaportes-sep-2-0) was launched in April 2026 under a four-year contract with a foreign state mint.
developments:
The system launched under a four-year contract with another country's national printing and minting house ([system](2026-04-15-stp-lanca-sistema-emissao-passaportes-sep-2-0)).

The predecessor system's status is not established in anything held, so what changed is unstated. Passport personalisation held under contract with a foreign state institution is a sovereignty arrangement the record states and does not examine.

summary: The central bank [launched a first financial technology sandbox](2025-06-03-bcstp-lanca-sandbox-fintechs-inclusao-financeira) under the national financial inclusion strategy, and no later update is held.
developments:
The sandbox was launched in June 2025 ([sandbox](2025-06-03-bcstp-lanca-sandbox-fintechs-inclusao-financeira)).

No cohort, admission, criteria or graduation is recorded since. It is the only payments instrument in this ledger apart from a donor grant active since 2017, so the country's entire digital payments record is a sandbox with no published cohort and a grant with an unexplained disbursement figure.

progress: Mixed, the first automatic roll derived from the civil registry while that derivation reproduced the register's own omissions
summary: The [automatic electoral roll](2026-07-31-eleicoes26-cen-lanca-campanha-de-consulta-e-atualizacao-de-dados) carries 146,510 voters for the September 2026 elections, added after a process failure that had missed about 1,860 eligible voters.
developments:
The reform project closed in September 2025, the new system was ready in February 2026 and automatic registration was inaugurated in April ([project](2025-09-02-stp-encerra-projeto-reforma-sistema-eleitoral-prese), [system](2026-02-06-stp-pronto-novo-sistema-recenseamento-eleitoral), [inauguration](2026-04-30-prese-inaugura-recenseamento-automatico)).

The provisional roll carries 146,510 voters, added after a fix to the process failure ([roll](2026-07-31-eleicoes26-cen-lanca-campanha-de-consulta-e-atualizacao-de-dados)).

The finding is what the failure was: the first automatic derivation from the civil registry reproduced that register's own omissions. Automating a derivation inherits the source's gaps, and the electoral commission launched a consultation and update campaign in response. The data-protection authority supervises the interconnection, which is recorded separately.

summary: The social protection directorate [stated a coverage figure for the single social registry](2026-08-03-direcao-da-protecao-social-esclarece-sobre-cadastro-social-unico-stp) and clarified that it is not a poverty count.
developments:
The clarification was issued in August 2026 ([clarification](2026-08-03-direcao-da-protecao-social-esclarece-sobre-cadastro-social-unico-stp), [mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

An agency publicly correcting a misreading of its own registry figure is unusual in this frame and worth recording as such: a registry count measures who is enrolled, not who is poor, and conflating the two misstates both.

No enrolment total, update cycle or link to the identity system is published.

summary: A [legal and technical diagnostic of the business registry](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) was presented toward a modern, data-oriented registry, and no later source is found.
developments:
The diagnostic findings were presented by a lender mission in September 2025 ([diagnostic](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

Nothing since. It is one of four items in this unit whose entire record is a single line in one donor mission report.

summary: [Computing equipment was handed over to the tax directorate](2026-08-18-rstp-sao-tome-pnud-equipamentos-direcao-geral-impostos) in August 2026, with no value or delivery schedule stated.
developments:
The handover was made with a United Nations development partner ([handover](2026-08-18-rstp-sao-tome-pnud-equipamentos-direcao-geral-impostos)).

No value for the equipment and no delivery schedule is stated, and no tax system, digitisation programme or revenue objective is named alongside it. Equipment arriving without a stated system is what most of this unit's government-technology record looks like.

summary: A [citizen portal](2026-03-28-inic-lanca-portal-do-cidadao) entered beta in March 2026, funded by a lender and a foundation with external technical advisory.
developments:
The beta was launched at the identity institute's eighteenth anniversary ([portal](2026-03-28-inic-lanca-portal-do-cidadao), [launch](2026-04-07 São Tomé and Príncipe Launches Citizen Portal)).

Two accounts frame the same launch differently — one as the institute's portal, the other as the lender and foundation's citizen portal — and they are treated here as one object.

No service count, user figure or exit-from-beta date is published. It sits on the same interoperability platform and digital identity prototypes recorded separately, none of which is confirmed delivered.

summary: An [integrated trade single window and customs system deployment](2026-01-25-salto-tecnologico-comercio-externo-janela-unica-asyfive) was announced with United Nations support in January 2026.
developments:
The announcement covers a port and external trade single window alongside a customs platform deployment ([announcement](2026-01-25-salto-tecnologico-comercio-externo-janela-unica-asyfive)).

No contract, value, timetable or go-live is published, and nothing has entered the base since. For an island economy dependent on port throughput, it is the highest-value government system announced in this period and the least evidenced.

summary: A [tender for 80 tablets and 90 desktops](2026-07-30-unicef-aquisicao-de-tablets-computadores-e-acessorios-sistema-educativo-stp) for school computer rooms closed in August 2026, under a national digital learning programme, alongside a [school connectivity plan](2025-01-25-cst-35-anos-expansao-rede-conectividade-escolas) announced in 2025.
developments:
The equipment tender was opened by a United Nations agency and closed on 12 August 2026 ([tender](2026-07-30-unicef-aquisicao-de-tablets-computadores-e-acessorios-sistema-educativo-stp), [procurement](2026-07-30-unicef-aquisicao-de-tablets-computadores-e-acessorios-sistema-educativo-stp)).

The operator's school connectivity plan would expand fibre and mobile to schools, larger schools first, working with the education ministry; it predates the window and no follow-up source is found ([plan](2025-01-25-cst-35-anos-expansao-rede-conectividade-escolas)).

One hundred and seventy devices is the whole of the country's school digital equipment programme on this record, and the connectivity that would make them useful is an unfollowed announcement.
